answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, ruling out negotiate_terms, and the contract expires in 14 days without auto-renew, ruling out defer_decision given the line is already running with no buffer (94% of committed volume). Renewing the incumbent fails the mandated 18% cost cut outright. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate and memory_c2 records a prior successful onboarding with accurate invoicing, but that memory is a single archived data point about cost and onboarding speed, not about performance under a tight, no-buffer production window, so I want to verify its original detail before committing fully. I also want to check memory_c1 to see whether the incumbent's stability record includes any resilience info relevant to comparing switching risk. Given the deadline forces a primary-vendor decision now, add_second_source doesn't address the expiring contract itself. I'm treating this as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because switching primary supply with no buffer and only one prior successful onboarding data point still carries real delivery-risk exposure that should be monitored closely rather than assumed resolved by a single past success.
